# Vendor credential shapes, which this repo's source must never contain.
#
# The rule these guard: sal never inspects a credential's CONTENTS to choose a
# DESTINATION. The destination comes out of the bank entry's manifest — `file`
# on the secret it declares — and nothing else.
#
# Matched as a case-insensitive SUBSTRING of a string literal, unlike
# bank-names.txt which is token-based. A prefix is only ever a prefix, so the
# thing to catch is "does this literal contain it at all".
#
# Why the rule needs a guard at all: sniffing a prefix looks harmless and reads
# as helpful — `sal` could "just know" that sk-ant-oat01- means the OAuth file
# and sk-ant-api03- means the API-key file. It is the same coupling as naming a
# bank entry, one level further in, and it fails worse: guessing wrong writes a
# credential into the file the broker reads for the OTHER one, which is silent
# at install and surfaces much later as a rejected request.
#
# The bank already answers this properly. A provider with two credential kinds
# declares two secrets with two files and two env vars, and which one the
# operator meant is settled by which prompt they answered.
#
# _test.go files are scanned too, which does catch realistic-looking test
# values. That is a deliberate choice and it has already fired once: test
# values are arbitrary, so the cheap fix is to make the fixture obviously fake.
# If it ever becomes a real nuisance, exempt _test.go — do NOT delete lines
# from this file, which would blind the check on production code as well.
#
# Anthropic
sk-ant-
# OpenAI-style, since a future bank entry may carry one
sk-proj-
# GitHub: personal, OAuth, user-to-server, server-to-server, refresh, fine-grained
ghp_
gho_
ghu_
ghs_
ghr_
github_pat_
# AWS access keys
AKIA
ASIA
# Slack
xoxb-
xoxp-
# Google API keys
AIza
# PEM armour, the shape most likely to be used as "is this a private key?"
